set.body:
DISTINCT FROM bd-01KZY9FGVJ0JXCB1Q1KN88AE6D, which is about citing the published variance expression. This is about a structural property of the two entry paths that no document states. Separated because the fixes are different: that one is a citation and a recipe, this one is a statement of what a path can and cannot support.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. A relation built from precomputed effects refuses every accessor needed for a correct standard error:

  effect_covariance          -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_block             -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_df                -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.
  residual_pair_statistics   -> ERROR: Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical.

EVERY REFUSAL IS CORRECT. The effect-coordinate covariance and the residual covariance are genuinely not recoverable from betas alone, and introduction.Rmd:359-362 already states in prose that a relation built only from precomputed effects cannot recreate information discarded upstream. The package behaves exactly as designed and the design is right.

THE CONSEQUENCE HAD NEVER BEEN DRAWN. On the lm_relation_fit() path the correct standard error IS computable from exported functions alone, and it works - intervals covering 0.94 to 0.99 against 0.57 to 0.74 for the naive alternative. On the precomputed-beta path there is no correct option inside the package at all.

And the precomputed-beta path is the DEFAULT EXPERIENCE. It is the README opening example, both vignettes, and the task the hands-on reviewer completed first. So:

  THE USERS WITH NO CORRECT WAY TO COMPUTE AN ERROR BAR ARE EXACTLY THE USERS MOST LIKELY
  TO REACH FOR AN INCORRECT ONE, AND THE INCORRECT ONE IS OVERCONFIDENT BY UP TO 3.2X.

This is not a defect and I am not filing it as one. It is a limitation that is correct, deliberate, and undocumented, presented to the user only as 'Relation-fit fields are missing or noncanonical' - which reads as a construction error rather than as a property of their chosen entry path. See the note on bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM.

WHAT TO STATE, and where:
  1. in ?relation and the introduction vignette: a relation built from precomputed effects
     carries no error channel, so residual-based quantities and correct standard errors are
     unavailable on this path; lm_relation_fit() retains them
  2. in the same place: on the precomputed-beta path, resample at the subject level rather
     than across partition-pairs
  3. rewrite the four accessor errors to name the cause and the constructor rather than
     reporting a field check

WHY THIS RANKS AS HIGH AS IT DOES. Every other documentation finding in this workstream costs a reader time. This one costs them correctness, silently, on the path the documentation itself steers them onto. It is the one place where the accessibility problem and the statistics problem are the same problem: the package leads with the easy path, and the easy path is the one where the obvious next step is wrong.
set.title: The precomputed-beta entry path forecloses correct uncertainty estimation, and never says so
